text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government says a clear "no" to bikers who are planning a huge protest in August to mark the deaths of two Greek Cypriots by Turks last year in a similar rally.
- The first round of direct talks between President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash expected to last 10 days in New York.
- Bikers will face the full force of the law if they attempt a mass protest along the green line in August.
- Justice Minister Nicos Koshis says rioting in central Nicosia on Monday night was not accidental, but planned.
- Rioting in Nicosia on Monday night is dynamite to the foundations of the Cyprus Republic, warns communist party chief Demetris Christofias.
- Shopkeepers will have to fork out and pay for damage caused to their shops by "blue wolves" on Monday.
- The Turks are getting ready for tough bargaining on territorial issues. They are seeking 37 percent and are citing old Ottoman documents relating to property.
- The Attorney-General is studying the possibility of disbanding the Cyprus Motorcyclists Federation (CMF) which is planning new demonstrations in August.
- Rockets used in a military exercise landed in somebody's garden in Pyrga village in the Larnaca district. The National Guard gives assurances it won't happen again.
- The Turks appear to be unyielding on territorial issues, though Nicosia will show some flexibility in the upcoming talks.
